title: Silver Is Down 19%. This Isn't What You Think.
speaker: Eric (Summit Metals)

macro_themes.view: Silver's 19% drop is mostly high yields (10y ~5.14%, 30y ~5.7%) and a strong dollar; funds prefer 5% bonds to non-yielding metal.
Fed meets Oct 27-28; ~17% October and ~80% December hike odds, and every move in those odds moves metals.
Algorithmic/CTA selling and daily leveraged-ETF rebalancing are amplifying the decline while commercials cover shorts.
Sixth straight year of silver deficit (~46M oz), though thrifting may flip it to surplus by 2027; Deutsche still sees ~$70 by mid-2027.
Believes the dollar will eventually succumb to pressure.

calls.condition: If silver gets back above 60-61 (20-day MA) and the 20-day crosses back over the 50-day, the selling is done and trend money returns; a weekly close below 55 makes him more cautious.
calls.reason: Below all moving averages with a bearish 20/50 cross short-term, but physical deficits, commercial short covering and central-bank buying support the long term.
calls.quote: If silver gets back above, say 60-61... That's the first sign the selling's done.

calls.reason: Gold held up better than silver (down ~12%); central banks buying dips; needs to reclaim the 20-day.
calls.quote: For gold, I just want to see it back above that 4180. That's its 20-day.

calls.reason: Dollar strong now but expected eventually to weaken under pressure.
calls.quote: I still believe that the dollar will eventually succumb to the pressure.

notes: Gold quoted as '41.37' in transcript, read as 4137. Date from listing; host says Fed meets 'next week, October 27th and 28th'. Advice is to stack small on a schedule, not make all-or-nothing moves.
